A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same collaborative pretraining-data-selection framework. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original 1.3B-model benchmark experiments, 373M-model ablations, and corpus and influence analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds larger-model experiments, 1.3B-model ablations, reference-task sensitivity tests, and computational-cost analyses.

M1.justification: The additive category-weight update in v1 Equation 5 becomes a sliding-average update in v3 Equation 5 and Appendix A.4.2. The three selection criteria, influence-based feedback, weighted console, and top-k selection remain. However, v3 Algorithm 2 retains the additive update, leaving the implemented procedure ambiguous.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SlimPajama/Common Crawl data, ten downstream benchmarks, and LAMBADA, SQuAD, and Jeopardy reference-task pool. Larger models and experiments using individual reference tasks change configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The external baseline roster in Table 1 and the full benchmark tables is unchanged. v3 Appendix A.4.3/Table 5 adds a mechanism comparison without actor collaboration, reporting a 35.0 average alongside dynamic and fixed collaboration; its connection to the discussed competitive mechanism is only briefly specified.

E3.justification: v3 adds 3.6B/8B model settings, 1.3B component ablations, and individual-reference-task controls, while retaining the original 373M ablation. Cost reporting changes from GPU hours to FLOPs. The added roughly 3B experiment has conflicting specifications: Appendix A.1 states 3.6B parameters and 36B tokens, whereas Table 3 states 3B parameters and 60B tokens.

E4.justification: v3 adds reference-task sensitivity testing (Table 8), component and dynamic-weight ablations at 1.3B scale (Table 2), the collaboration-mechanism comparison (Table 5), and detailed offline/online cost analysis (Table 6). The original 373M ablation survives as Table 7, and the existing influence and distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark accuracy results. The added tables retain point-estimate reporting, and the existing regression/Spearman plots are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1, the full zero-/three-/five-shot benchmark results, and the original 373M ablation retain their numerical values. v3 adds larger-model method/random averages of 30.7/27.0 and 34.6/31.4 (Tables 3–4), new ablation results, reference-task averages spanning 37.2–37.7, and FLOP estimates. These extend the results under newly reported settings.

T1.justification: v3 separates the per-sample influence proxy r from the dataset reward R, replacing v1's conflated expression. It also changes the cross-actor reward average from division by k to division by three actors. Appendix A.4 largely reformulates existing optimization definitions through an RL interpretation; it adds no theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: dynamically combining selection criteria resolves conflicts, improves data efficiency and convergence, and achieves up to 10.5% average improvement. Renaming agents as actors and specifying relative improvement clarify the presentation without materially changing those claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds a bias–variance explanation for sliding-average updates, distinctions between competitive and collaborative mechanisms, an interpretation of reference-task insensitivity, and extrapolation toward models above 10B parameters. Its new Limitations section explicitly bounds the evidence by the tested 8B scale and restricted token budgets.

D1.justification: v3 adds larger-model architecture specifications, new-criterion integration instructions, and computational-cost details, and changes the advertised repository address. It drops v1's explicit 373M 8-GPU/5,000-step description and Table 1's per-task shot mapping. Table 9 also reverses the earlier smaller-model hidden-size and attention-head assignments, introducing reproducibility ambiguity.

R1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.4 substantially reposition the framework as specialized criterion actors with a shared objective, distinguishing it from autonomous-agent systems and relating it to MARL and multi-actor planning. References to Ligtenberg et al. (2001, 2004) and Wang et al. (2020) support this expanded positioning.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, abstract, introduction, contribution summaries, definitions, and ablation narrative are revised. Detailed initialization and the training algorithm move into the appendix, which is reorganized extensively; separate limitations and acknowledgements sections are added.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document to a two-column layout, redesigns and relocates Figure 1, redraws explanatory diagrams, and moves the classifier pipeline and training algorithm into the appendix. It adds several experimental tables and an integration algorithm and expands the architecture table. Most existing empirical plots are reused.

improvement.justification: The new 1.3B ablations, reference-task sensitivity tests, and larger-model results strengthen support for the retained framework, while the positioning and applicability limits become clearer. The net gain is constrained by reporting inconsistencies: Equation 5 disagrees with Algorithm 2, Appendix A.1 conflicts with Table 3's training budget, and Table 9 reverses smaller-model configuration assignments. These defects limit the reproducibility of the expanded evidence.
